## In-process

![](img/schema.png){width="100%"}



:::{.notes}
Different from classical architecture client/server 

- client: send requests to the server and get back the result  
- server: run continuously, receives requests, analyse and determine an execution plan  
- stockage: usually, local system file of the server  

In duckdb: 
the client and the server run in the same process that only runs for the time of the duckdb session
the data storage is decoupled from duckdb that works by default `in-memory` and take external data sources 

* Architecture classique (type postgres) : client => serveur / stockage des données  
* Architecture Duckdb : client / serveur => sources multiples de données
:::

---

## Analytical

</br>

Specialized in analytical treatments (opposed as transactionnal) :

</br>

- Use of raw data (.csv, .parquet, .json)

- Mainly use WORM `write once, read many` pattern (read the data than modifying it) 

---

## Interoperability

</br>

- Read and interface multiple data sources (csv, parquet, geoparquet, json...)

- Several protocols (s3, http, databases...)

- Compatible with PostgreSQL dialect (almost entirely)

![](img/interoperability.png){width="100%"}


---

## Portable

</br>

- Multiple languages and multiple plateforme 

</br>

We will now focus on the R client, and the cli but there are many other ways to use it : R, python, Rust, Java, web assembly...

##

un mot sur la ram - disk
disk vs memory ? OUI & OOM 
comment gérer si trop gros



Most DuckDB internals are optimized for in-memory operation. By
default, 80% of the host RAM1 is used to process data and queries.
Memory  is a precious resource. DuckDB is built to use all RAM
available but gradually moves to disk-based processing if required
(out-of-core processing):
If queries permit, stream small data chunks (packs of vectors)
through the system. Avoid to materialize entire tables in RAM.
Try to hold intermediate data structures (e.g., hash tables) in
memory. Spill to disk if a query produces huge intermediates.
In the remaining memory space (if any), cache disk-resident table
data to speed up future accesses.
DB lingo: buffering


uckDB temporarily uses out-of-core memory on disk to hold (parts
of) large intermediates (DB lingo: spilling).


As long as memory usage permits, DuckDB buffers data read from
persistent database file *.db file in RAM:


DuckDB uses column-based storage j for base tables, but relies on
a row-major layout k for paged intermediate data:
Co-locating the columns of a row helps row comparison during
sorting, hashing, or joins (column access locality).

## Meet the terminal

### Install the cli 

Demo

---


DuckDB CLI est distribué sous forme de binaire standalone, téléchargeable directement sur [leur site documentaire](https://duckdb.org/docs/installation/?version=stable&environment=cli&platform=linux&download_method=direct&architecture=x86_64).  
Il est par ailleurs préinstallé dans la majorité des environnements modernes de datascience dont les environnements lancés par [Onyxia](https://onyxia.sh)

## Première utilisation de la cli

Lancer `duckdb` :  

```shell
ines@laboitemagique:~$ duckdb
v1.3.0 (Ossivalis) 71c5c07cdd
Enter ".help" for usage hints.
Connected to a transient in-memory database.
Use ".open FILENAME" to reopen on a persistent database.
```  

On constate bien que `duckdb` travaille uniquement en mémoire (`transient in-memory database`). Toutes les données seront donc perdues à la fin de la session.  
Si on veut qu'il sauvegarde ses tables, on peut préciser un fichier de database au moment du lancement `duckdb madb.db` ou à chaud pendant une session : `.open madb.db`.  

---

## Let's make the CLI less serious  

To configure the CLI, create a file  `.duckdbrc` at the root of your personnal repo ($HOME)
This file is executed at the duckdb session's startup

```
.prompt '🦆'
.timer on
```


---

## Let's try it 🚀

```
duckdb
> some sql command 

```
-> see the version and that it is in memory 
and then do SQL

or you can execute a file too

```
duckdb -f demo.sql 
```

## Tip 
</br>
Use another client before using duckdb R (or create a directory), else, you will install extensions twice, define secrets twice...  
</br>
By default things are installed/configured in a temporary file. To avoid that:  
Create the directory   
~/.duckdb
  
Or use the CLI or another client before using duckdb-r

## Give the cli a try 

![](img/logo.png){width="100%"}


::: {.notes}


Replaces the marker-file storage mechanism (and the per-kind directory options/env vars) with a single home directory for DuckDB's downloaded extensions and stored secrets, resolved fresh on every duckdb() call that creates a new driver. Implements the design converged with CRAN (Kurt Hornik) on the "duckdb default storage location" thread: use ~/.duckdb if it already exists, never create it non-interactively, and offer to create it interactively.

Extensions live at <home>/extensions, secrets at <home>/stored_secrets.

:::
